title: The Token Games: Evaluating Language Model Reasoning with Puzzle Duels
abstract: arXiv:2602.17831v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Evaluating the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models is increasingly challenging as models improve. Human curation of hard questions is highly expensive, especially in recent benchmarks using PhD-level domain knowledge to challenge the most capable models. Even then, there is always a concern about whether these questions test genuine reasoning or if similar problems have been seen during training. Here, we take inspiration from 16th-century mathematical duels to design The Token Games (TTG): an evaluation framework where models challenge each other by creating their own puzzles. We leverage the format of Programming Puzzles - given a function that returns a boolean, find inputs that make it return True - to flexibly represent problems and enable verifying solutions. translated_title: 令牌游戏：通过谜题对决评估语言模型推理能力
translated_abstract: 随着模型能力的不断提升，评估大型语言模型的推理能力变得越来越具有挑战性。人工策划难题的成本极高，尤其是在近期一些使用博士级领域知识来挑战最强模型的基准测试中。即便如此，人们始终担心这些问题是否真正测试了推理能力，或者类似问题是否在训练期间已被模型见过。在此，我们从16世纪的数学对决中汲取灵感，设计了The Token Games（TTG）：一个让模型通过自主创建谜题来相互挑战的评估框架。我们利用编程谜题的形式——给定一个返回布尔值的函数，找到使其返回True的输入——来灵活地表示问题并实现对解答的验证。利用两两对决的结果，我们计算Elo评分，从而能够在模型之间进行相对比较。我们在TTG上评估了10个前沿模型……
tldr: 该论文提出了The Token Games（TTG）评估框架，让语言模型通过自主创建编程谜题并两两对决来评估推理能力，并利用Elo评分实现前沿模型间的相对比较。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes The Token Games (TTG), an evaluation framework where language models challenge each other by creating their own programming puzzles, with Elo ratings used to compare the reasoning capabilities of frontier models.
